reasoning_summary: The deterministic verdict is INCONCLUSIVE with no failed checks, so ACCEPT and REJECT are both ruled out. Mesh, time and domain uncertainty are unmeasured for both quantities (R0).

R0 averaging and statistics components are measured and tiny. For drag they are 9.366e-05 and 8.229e-05. For Strouhal they are 1.551e-05 and 6.605e-05. Averaging and statistics are not the limiting factor, so RUN_LONGER would add little.

R0 completed (15000 steps, max Courant 0.73373). It has 12 stationary cycles and 611.87 steps per shedding period. Mass imbalance is 8.3333e-11, and the checks for linear-solver convergence, Reynolds consistency and force reference all pass. Together these make time-step error less likely to be the dominant error than spatial error.

R0 spatial resolution is the weakest recorded point. The representative cell size is 0.45745 D on 30580 cells, and the last wake cell is 1.0209 D. Wake resolution controls shedding frequency and the mean drag. Strouhal number and drag could therefore shift by more than 3% on refinement.
The domain is 30 D upstream, 50 D downstream and 40 D half-height, with blockage ratio 0.0125. It is already fairly large, so domain error is a lower-priority hypothesis than mesh error.

REFINE_MESH from R0 is the most informative single experiment. It addresses both requested quantities. It costs 1779 s, and the budget allows 6 experiments and 12x the root compute, with none used so far.
missing_evidence: Mesh discretisation error for mean_drag_coefficient and strouhal_number (no REFINE_MESH run)
Temporal discretisation error for both quantities (no REDUCE_TIME_STEP run)
Domain truncation/blockage error for both quantities (no EXPAND_DOMAIN run)
Combined uncertainty against the 0.03 tolerance for both quantities

hypotheses.hypothesis: R0 wake and far-field resolution (representative cell size 0.45745 D, last wake cell 1.0209 D) is too coarse. The mean drag or Strouhal number would then change by more than 1.5% under systematic refinement.
hypotheses.test: REFINE_MESH from R0 with factor 1.4142. Compare the stationary-window mean_drag_coefficient (R0: 1.3311) and strouhal_number (R0: 0.16343). A relative change below 1.5% for both supports mesh adequacy. A change above 3% is a FAIL.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Domain truncation (blockage 0.0125, symmetry lateral boundaries) biases the results by less than 1.5%.
hypotheses.test: A later EXPAND_DOMAIN run from R0, if mesh error is acceptable.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Time-step error is small at 0.01 convective units (about 612 steps per period, Courant 0.73373).
hypotheses.test: A later REDUCE_TIME_STEP run from R0 with factor 2.

next_experiment.reason: Mesh error is the largest unmeasured component and the most likely to move the mean drag or Strouhal number by more than the 3% tolerance. R0 has a coarse representative cell size (0.45745 D) and a coarse far wake (last cell 1.0209 D). The other recorded components (averaging, statistics, Courant, mass balance, solver residuals) are already well controlled.
next_experiment.expected_outcome: If both quantities change by less than about 1.5% relative to R0 (drag 1.3311, Strouhal 0.16343), the mesh component passes and the next experiments are EXPAND_DOMAIN and REDUCE_TIME_STEP. If either changes by more than 3%, the verifier records a FAIL for R0. A change between 1.5% and 3% would call for a second refinement to confirm convergence.
